memory_candidates.content: Lean 4's `/- -/` block comments nest arbitrarily, so no `grep`/regex filter chain can correctly strip them (nesting is not a regular language). A single-pass, depth-counting character-scan stripper (python3) that tracks comment depth and string-literal state, preserving newlines in place of stripped content, correctly handles nested block comments, `--` line comments, `/-- -/` docstrings, and string literals while keeping line numbers aligned with the original file. Mask (rather than preserve) string-literal interiors with spaces if the goal is a content-based keyword scan (e.g. `sorry` census) so keywords appearing only as string text are correctly excluded.

For an opt-in compiler cross-check flag that reuses `lake build` output (e.g. `--cross-check` invoking `lake build 2>&1 | grep -c "declaration uses 'sorry'"`), make the flag self-contained (run its own `lake build` inside the check) rather than assuming a build already ran earlier in the same call site's step sequence -- call-site step ordering varies across agents (some run the build before the check, some after) and a self-contained flag works correctly regardless.

In this repo's .claude/ extension deployment model: deployed cslib agents in .claude/agents/ are symlinks into .claude/extensions/cslib/agents/, so editing extension-source auto-propagates (verify with `readlink`). lean agents are NOT deployed to .claude/agents/ in this repo. install-extension.sh deploys agents/commands/skills but NOT scripts -- .claude/scripts/ is a real, version-controlled directory that is the canonical home for shared scripts referenced by any agent; for extension-packaging completeness, place a source-of-truth copy in the owning extension's scripts/ dir and register it in that extension's manifest.json provides.scripts.
